classification.difficultyReason: Transform the domain, select both cosine solutions, undo the shift and locate them on the supplied graph.

content.prompt: Solve $2\cos\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=1$ algebraically in the domain $[0,2\pi]$ and indicate the solutions on the graph.

spec.description: Cosine curve with filled endpoints, labelled axes and quarter-period labels; unlabelled horizontal ticks occur every pi/6. No grid.
spec.mathematics: y=2 cos(x-pi/6), 0<=x<=2pi; maximum 2 at x=pi/6; endpoints (0,sqrt3) and (2pi,sqrt3); vertical ticks at -2,-1,1,2.
spec.answerVisibility: Curve and axes supplied; solution markings hidden.

answer.worked:
Let $u=x-\frac{\pi}{6}$. The transformed domain is $-\frac{\pi}{6}\le u\le\frac{11\pi}{6}$.
$$\begin{align*}2\cos u&=1\\\cos u&=\frac12\\u&=\frac{\pi}{3},\ \frac{5\pi}{3}\\x&=u+\frac{\pi}{6}\\x&=\frac{\pi}{2},\ \frac{11\pi}{6}.\end{align*}$$
Draw $y=1$ and mark its intersections with the supplied curve.

spec.description: Solution overlay with the identical coordinate units and bounding box as the question graph. A dashed horizontal line and marked intersections indicate both solutions.
spec.mathematics: Intersections of y=2 cos(x-pi/6) with y=1 at x=pi/2 and x=11pi/6.
